title: Fewest monochromatic triangles in the E8 root graph
statement: Let G be the graph on the 240 roots of E8, two roots adjacent when their inner product is 1 (6720 edges, 60480 triangles; every edge lies in 27 triangles and every vertex neighbourhood is the Gosset graph). Colour each edge red or blue. What is the least possible number of monochromatic triangles? Known: 10080 <= minimum <= 10385; find a colouring with fewer than 10385 monochromatic triangles, or improve the lower bound.
submission: Text file: 6720 digits 0 or 1, the colours of the edges in the checker's order (roots doubled to integer vectors and sorted; edges (a, b), a < b, in lexicographic order; see e8_edges in checkers/orig_comb.py).
score: the number of monochromatic triangles (smaller is better)

best_known.source: Quantavane (Arhan Canli), 9 November 2026: simulated annealing over edge colourings, each move scored by the 27 triangles through the edge (tools/mono_triangles.py, 1500 sweeps)

context: Goodman's theorem (1959) gives the exact minimum number of monochromatic triangles in a 2-colouring of the complete graph, and Ramsey multiplicity problems ask the same for other graphs; on host graphs other than complete graphs the minimum is a property of the host. The E8 root graph is the most symmetric dense graph in eight dimensions (its automorphism group is the Weyl group W(E8), of order 696,729,600). A local version of Goodman's count gives a lower bound: a triangle that is not monochromatic has exactly two vertices where its two edges differ in colour, and at a vertex v those pairs are the cut edges of a 2-colouring of the Gosset graph on N(v), whose maximum cut is exactly 420 (an eigenvalue bound that a configuration attains); so at least 60480 - 240 * 420 / 2 = 10080 triangles are monochromatic. Equality would need every neighbourhood split by a maximum cut at once; our best colouring has 10385.
references: A. W. Goodman, On sets of acquaintances and strangers at any party, Amer. Math. Monthly 66 (1959) 778-783
J. H. Conway, N. J. A. Sloane, Sphere Packings, Lattices and Groups (Springer, 1999), chapter 4 (the E8 root system)
B. Mohar, S. Poljak, Eigenvalues and the max-cut problem, Czechoslovak Math. J. 40 (1990) 343-352

novelty.verdict: new. No study of monochromatic triangles (or Ramsey multiplicity) in edge colourings of the E8 root graph was found on arXiv; Goodman-type problems are studied for complete graphs and random or pseudo-random hosts.
closest: Goodman's theorem and Ramsey multiplicity on complete graphs; the host graph here is the E8 root graph, and the bound and the answer differ.

baseline.text: 10385, held by Quantavane (Arhan Canli), 9 November 2026: the colouring in `refs/e8-goodman.txt`. Lower bound 10080 from the local count above, using the exact maximum cut 420 of the Gosset graph (our configuration attains its eigenvalue bound 56 (27 + 3) / 4 = 420).

bound.source: 60480 - (1/2) * 240 * 420: each vertex sees at most 420 bichromatic pairs (the maximum cut of the Gosset graph)
